The percentage of patients achieving sustained virologic response at 12 weeks (SVR12) was 92%, with a GRADE assessment of high certainty. A detailed summary of the analyses is presented in the referenced section. 2. In the analysis of all-treatment-experienced patients treated with glecaprevir and pibrentasvir, evidence was available for patients with genotypes 1, 2, 4-6, as well as those with unknown or mixed genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 83% to 99%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high across outcomes. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 3. No evidence was available for treatment-naïve patients treated with glecaprevir and pibrentasvir. Similarly, no evidence was available for treatment-experienced patients treated with the same regimen. 4. In the analysis of all-treatment-experienced patients with cirrhosis treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1, 3, 4, and 6, as well as unknown or mixed genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 58% to 97%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 5. For treatment-naïve patients with cirrhosis treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1, 4, and 6, as well as unknown or mixed genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 85% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 6. For treatment-experienced patients with cirrhosis treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1 and 6, as well as unknown or mixed genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 83% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 7. In the analysis of all-treatment-experienced patients with cirrhosis treated with paritaprevir/ritonavir, ombitasvir, and dasabuvir, evidence was available only for genotype 1. The SVR12 rate was 99% in both trial-only and all-evidence analyses, with a GRADE assessment of high certainty. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 8. No evidence was identified for treatment-naïve patients with cirrhosis treated with paritaprevir/ritonavir, ombitasvir, and dasabuvir. Similarly, no evidence was available for treatment-experienced patients treated with the same regimen. 9. In the analysis of all-treatment-experienced patients with cirrhosis treated with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1-4 and 6, as well as unknown or mixed genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 75% to 97%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 10. For treatment-naïve patients with cirrhosis treated with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir, evidence was available only for genotype 3. The GRADE assessment was high. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 11. For treatment-experienced patients with cirrhosis treated with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir, evidence was available for genotype 2, as well as unknown or mixed genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 86% to 90%, with a GRADE assessment of moderate certainty. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 12. In the analysis of all-treatment-experienced patients with cirrhosis treated with sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir, evidence was available for genotypes 1 and 3, as well as unknown or mixed genotypes. The SVR12 rates ranged from 95% to 96%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 13. For treatment-naïve patients with cirrhosis treated with sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir, evidence was available only for genotype 3. The GRADE assessment was moderate. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 14. For treatment-experienced patients with cirrhosis treated with sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir, evidence was available for genotypes 1 and 3, as well as unknown or mixed genotypes. The GRADE assessments varied from very low to high. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 15. The literature review for daclatasvir, sofosbuvir, and ribavirin was restricted to patients with cirrhosis and genotype 2 or 3 infections. No evidence was identified for genotype 2. For genotype 3, the pooled SVR12 rates ranged from 86% to 91%, with a GRADE assessment of low certainty. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 16. For treatment-naïve patients with cirrhosis treated with daclatasvir, sofosbuvir, and ribavirin, evidence was available only for genotype 3. The pooled SVR12 rates ranged from 83% to 98%, with a GRADE assessment of very low certainty. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 17. For treatment-experienced patients with cirrhosis treated with daclatasvir, sofosbuvir, and ribavirin, evidence was available only for genotype 3. From a single clinical trial (N=30), the SVR12 rate was 87%, with a GRADE assessment of low certainty. No observational studies were identified to support this analysis. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 18. The literature review for sofosbuvir and ribavirin was restricted to patients with cirrhosis and genotype 2 or 3 infections. Evidence was available for genotypes 2 and 3, as well as a single study reporting these groups together. The pooled SVR12 rates ranged from 61% to 86%, with a GRADE assessment of low certainty. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 19. For treatment-naïve patients with cirrhosis treated with sofosbuvir and ribavirin, evidence was available for genotypes 2 and 3, as well as a single study reporting these groups together. The pooled SVR12 rates ranged from 61% to 85%, with a GRADE assessment of low certainty. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 20. For treatment-experienced patients with cirrhosis treated with sofosbuvir and ribavirin, evidence was available for genotypes 2 and 3. The pooled SVR12 rates ranged from 57% to 82%, with GRADE assessments varying from low to moderate. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 21. In patients with HIV co-infection treated with elbasvir and grazoprevir, evidence was available for genotypes 1, 4, and 6, as well as unknown or mixed genotypes. The pooled SVR12 rates ranged from 83% to 96%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to moderate. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 22. In patients with HIV co-infection treated with glecaprevir and pibrentasvir, evidence was available only for unknown or mixed genotypes from a single observational study. The SVR12 rate was 100%, with a GRADE assessment of high certainty. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 23. In patients with HIV co-infection treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1 and 4, as well as unknown or mixed genotypes. The pooled SVR12 rates ranged from 75% to 98%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to high. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 24. In patients with HIV co-infection treated with paritaprevir/ritonavir, ombitasvir, and dasabuvir, evidence was available only for genotype 1 from an observational study. The SVR12 rate was 86%, with a GRADE assessment of very low certainty, largely due to the small sample size (N=7). A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 25. In patients with HIV co-infection treated with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir, evidence was available for genotypes 1-4. The pooled SVR12 rates ranged from 92% to 96%, with GRADE assessments varying from very low to low. A summary of the analyses is provided in the referenced section. 26. No evidence was available for treatment-naïve patients with HIV co-infection treated with sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir. Similarly, no evidence was available for treatment-experienced patients with HIV co-infection treated with the same regimen. 27. Safety outcomes were pooled across studies for each treatment, including the number of patients experiencing adverse events. Comparative evidence was not available, and inferences on relative treatment effects should be avoided. Evidence on discontinuations due to adverse events was available for all treatments. Analyses for daclatasvir, sofosbuvir, and ribavirin, as well as sofosbuvir and ribavirin, were restricted to patients with cirrhosis and genotypes 2 or 3.
